t: You're looking at Hanover Lodge, a Grade Two star listed house at 150 Park Road, overlooking Regent's Park. John Nash designed it, the architect behind many important parts of London, and it was built for General Sir Robert Arbuthnot, a commander in the Napoleonic Wars, who died here. Mary Carus-Wilson, an author and speaker on biblical study and missionary work, also died here. The house was later part of Bedford College and the French ambassador's residence. Today it's known for its price. The Russian businessman Andrey Goncharenko bought the lease in 2012 for 120 million pounds.
